2.name: Bangladesh - Population Movement (MDRBD018)
2.summary: Eight years after the large-scale displacement from Rakhine State, Myanmar in 2017, the humanitarian crisis in Cox’s Bazar remains one of the world’s most protracted and critically underfunded emergencies. As of 31 December 2025, nearly 1.18 million displaced people reside in 33 highly congested camps across Cox’s Bazar and Bhasan Char, with limited freedom of movement, restricted access to livelihoods, and continued reliance on humanitarian assistance.

5854.name: Ukraine and Impacted Countries
5854.summary: Four years into the international armed conflict between the Russian Federation and Ukraine, humanitarian needs inside Ukraine remain extensive, multi-layered, and deeply affected by ongoing hostilities. Civilian infrastructure has been regularly damaged, leading to sustained disruption of essential services and compounding the impact of armed violence on households already coping with displacement, loss of income, and repeated exposure to trauma.

6346.name: Syria: Earthquake - 2023-02
6346.summary: On 6 February at 4:17 am, a 7.8 degrees magnitude earthquake struck southern Turkey near Syria’s northern border. The US Geological Survey said the earthquake was centered about 33 km (20 miles) from Gaziantep, a major city and provincial capital. Tremors were felt as far away as Lebanon, Greece, Palestine, and the island of Cyprus. Another big earthquake was felt on the same day at around 1:24 pm local time, largely in the same affected areas.

6365.name: KEN: Drought - 2023-02
6365.summary: The IFRC Disaster Response Emergency Fund (DREF) has approved a total of CHF 499,199 for the Kenya Red Cross. The approved amount consists of an allocation of CHF 135,978 for readiness and prepositioning and CHF 363,222 allocated to implement early actions once the defined triggers are met. Allocations are made from the Anticipatory Pillar of the DREF, under the DREF appeal code MDR00001.

6414.name: Sudan Crisis - Complex Emergency Sudan
6414.summary: Sudan was plunged into a dire humanitarian crisis as a result of armed conflict. In the early morning of 15 April 2023, Khartoum woke up to the sound of gunfire and explosions. This was the first time that Sudan’s capital city was at the epicentre of a fierce conflict between two powerful groups, the Sudan Armed Forces (SAF) and the Rapid Support Forces (RSF).

6479.name: Sudan Crisis: Population Movement Neighbouring Countries
6479.summary: The Sudan conflict does not stop at the border. Due to the increase of the significant cross-border population movements out of Sudan as a result of the ongoing conflict and the deepening humanitarian crisis, the IFRC has revised the Emergency Appeal to support the humanitarian response of National Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies in neighbouring countries — Chad, Egypt, Ethiopia, South Sudan, Uganda, Central African Republic (CAR) and Libya.

6646.name: Morocco - Earthquake-2023-09
6646.summary: Please click here to view all IFRC interviews about the Moroccan earthquake. Overview An earthquake with a 6.8 magnitude shook Morocco on 8 September 2023, at 11 p.m. local time. According to the US Geological Survey (USGS), the quake originated at a depth of18.5km below the surface. Its epicentre was identified in the High Atlas Mountains, located 71km south-west of the city of Marrakesh, a major economic center.

6654.name: ETH:Drought(EAP)
6654.summary: Recurring droughts and floods have the most severe impact on Ethiopia’s population and the country has a long history of recurring droughts, which have increased in magnitude, frequency, and impact since the 1970s. The pastoral and agro-pastoral communities in drought prone areas, increasing aridity and recurring drought conditions present the most significant climate hazard.

6700.name: Middle East Crisis | MENA
6700.summary: REGIONAL OVERVIEW Since 7 October 2023, hostilities have significantly escalated across the Gaza Strip and the West Bank, leading to a severe humanitarian crisis in the occupied Palestinian territories (oPt) and surrounding countries. As of July 2026, the Middle East crisis remains highly volatile. Although the October 2025 Gaza ceasefire reduced hostilities, humanitarian needs in Gaza and the West Bank remains severe.

6886.name: DRC : Population Movement - 2024
6886.summary: Since the beginning of 2024, an intensification of the conflict between the armed forces of the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) and their allies against M23 rebel group has had devastating effects on civilians in several towns within North Kivu. Notably, the towns of Mweso, Bambo, Katsiru, Sake, and Goma have been severely impacted.

6924.name: Bangladesh: Cyclone EAP 2024
6924.summary: The IFRC Disaster Response Emergency Fund (DREF) has approved a total of CHF 499,987 for the implementation of the Bangladesh Red Crescent Society (BDRCS) cyclone EAP. The approved amount consists of an allocation of CHF 185,858 for readiness, CHF 112,958 for prepositioning and CHF 201,172 allocated to implement early actions once the defined triggers are met. Allocations are made from the Anticipatory Pillar of the DREF, under the DREF appeal code MDR00001.

6962.name: MRT: Population displacement - 04-2024 - Mauritania: Population movement in the Hodh El Chargui region in 2024
6962.summary: The humanitarian crisis that has affected Mali since 2012 has generated massive displacement of populations, both inside and outside the country, with significant repercussions on neighbouring countries, including Mauritania, Burkina Faso and Niger. Since 2012, tens of thousands of Malians have fled to Mauritania for safety due to instability and violence in their country.

7081.name: PHL: Cyclone - 07-2024 - Southwest Monsoon Enhanced by Typhoon Carina
7081.summary: The Southwest Monsoon which has been causing widespread flooding in Mindanao since 11 July, continues to affect the western parts of Southern Luzon, Visayas, and Mindanao. On Friday afternoon, July 19, PAGASA observe two low-pressure areas within the Philippine Area of Responsibility (PAR). At 3 PM, one LPA was 365 kilometers west of Tanauan City, Batangas, while the other was 865 kilometers east of the Eastern Visayas.

7082.name: Sudan : Floods & Cholera
7082.summary: Heavy rains since May 2024, combined with overflowing Lake Victoria, have caused the Nile River to burst its banks and with severe flooding, submerging villages, and farmland. As of 29 November, the situation remains critical with more than 1.4 million people affected in 44 of the country’s 78 counties (OCHA). On 28 October 2024, the Government of South Sudan declared a cholera outbreak in Renk, marking the start of a growing health crisis.

7162.name: SOM: Drought EAP
7162.summary: The IFRC Disaster Response Emergency Fund (DREF) has approved a total of CHF 492,619 for the implementation of the Somali Red Crescent Society (SRCS) Drought EAP. The approved amount consists of an allocation of CHF 157,431 for readiness and prepositioning and CHF 373,102 allocated to implement early actions once the defined triggers are met. Allocations are made from the Anticipatory Pillar of the DREF, under the DREF appeal code MDR00001.

7203.name: Lebanon Complex Emergency - 2024
7203.summary: On 2 March 2026, Lebanon experienced a major escalation in hostilities marked by intense airstrikes across South Lebanon, Nabatieh, Beirut’s southern suburbs, Bekaa, Baalbek-El Hermel, and Mount Lebanon. The escalation followed displacement warnings issued for more than 50 villages, triggering widespread civilian movement and placing significant pressure on essential services and humanitarian systems. The escalation occurred within an already fragile context.

7251.name: SYR: Complex Emergency - 11-2024 -
7251.summary: The escalating hostilities that have recently occurred in the northern governorates of Syria, specifically Aleppo, Idlib, and Hama, have led to the displacement of approximately 500,000 individuals inside and outside these governorates in search of safety and protection.

7431.name: ECU: 2025 Floods and environmental pollution
7431.summary: Since January 2025, Ecuador has been experiencing an increasingly complex emergency situation resulting from the convergence of two large-scale crises: a prolonged rainy season with intense floods and landslides, and a major environmental emergency caused by an oil spill in the coastal province of Esmeraldas. According to the Secretariat for Risk Management (SitRep No.

7459.name: CMR: Cholera EAP
7459.summary: Cameroon faces recurrent cholera outbreaks, exacerbated by seasonal floods, inadequate WASH (Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene) infrastructure, and rapid urbanization. Historical outbreaks, such as the 2021–2022 epidemic, which recorded 6,652 suspected cases and 132 deaths, highlightvulnerabilities in high-risk regions like Littoral, Southwest, and Center. Climate change and population displacement further amplify the risks, making early intervention crucial.

7461.name: TZA: Flood - 03-2025 - High rainfall and strong wind
7461.summary: Between March 21-24, 2025, heavy rainfall and strong winds severely impacted Musoma (Mara Region) and Ulanga (Morogoro Region), causing widespread destruction, displacement, and urgent humanitarian needs. In Musoma, storms damaged 524 households, destroying 165 houses and leaving 65 people in temporary shelters.

7464.name: Myanmar Earthquake March 2025
7464.summary: Myanmar Red Cross Society (MRCS) Response (as of 30 September 2025) and the IFRC network’s support Since the earthquake, MRCS has reached more than 200,000 people across 30 townships with the support from the Movement partners and external partners. More than 99,359 people have received health care, and more than 1.3 million liters of safe drinking water have been distributed.

figures.label: Fed-wide funding ask incld. bilateral support(CHF)

7468.name: Afghanistan: Population Movement, 2025
7468.summary: The recent deadline imposed to expel approximately 1.5 million Afghan nationals by end of 2025 has significantly deteriorated the humanitarian landscape, primarily along the formal border crossing points in Torkham and Spin Boldak (Nangarhar and Kandahar provinces). The initially imposed deadline, which ended on March 31, 2024, has forced many families to return to Afghanistan, resulting in a considerable influx of returnees, with a spike on April 5, 2025.

7505.name: SOM: Epidemic - 03-2025 - Leishmaniasis Outbreak
7505.summary: Since January 3, 2025, Erigavo Regional Hospital in the Sanaag region has reported five cases of leishmaniasis, a disease not historicallyprevalent in those areas of Somaliland. Among these cases, four tested positive for Leishmania IgG through Rapid Diagnostic Tests (RDTs),raising concerns about the potential emergence of a localized outbreak.

7550.name: Pakistan: Monsoon Flood, 2025
7550.summary: Since 26 June 2025, heavy monsoon rains have caused severe flash flooding across Pakistan including Gilgit Baltistan (GB), Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJ&K), while Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP) province being among the worst aected. The districts of Buner, Swat, Shangla, Mansehra and Swabi have suered extensive loss of life, widespread damage to infrastructure, and disruption of essential services.

7597.name: Fiji: Tropical Cyclone sEAP, 2025
7597.summary: Fiji is one of the world’s most vulnerable nations to climate change and climate-related disasters. The country is exposed to multiple hazards including earthquakes, tsunami, landslide, coastal flooding, tropical cyclones, and wildfire. One of the principal hazards affecting Fiji is tropical cyclones (TCs). Since 1969, there have been 33 TCs (Category 1 or higher) that have passed within 10 km of Fiji, and 16 that made landfall .

7598.name: Bangladesh: Cold Wave EAP, 2025
7598.summary: Though Bangladesh is in a subtropical monsoon region, due to being situated close to the Himalayan, the northern especially north-western part of Bangladesh faces extreme weather conditions during winter. Bangladesh has recently been experiencing cold waves, which often result in adverse impacts on the livelihoods of the most vulnerable people.

7601.name: Timor Leste: Flood sEAP, 2025
7601.summary: The frequent occurrence of extreme weather and climate events poses a great threat to community and national level development in Timor-Leste as their impacts cause catastrophic loss and damage. Timor-Leste is prone to natural hazards such as floods, landslides, drought, cyclones and earthquakes. Of these hazards, the most common is flood, followed by drought and storms . With its shoreline of more than 700 km, nearly 65 percent of the population resides in low-lying areas.

7602.name: Indonesia: Flood EAP, 2025
7602.summary: The IFRC Disaster Response Emergency Fund (DREF) has approved a total of CHF 517,485 for the implementationof the Indonesian Red Cross (Palang Merah Indonesia) Floods EAP. The approved amount consists of an allocation of CHF 316,873 for readiness and prepositioning and CHF 200,612 allocated to implement early actions once the defined triggers are met. Allocations are made from the Anticipatory Pillar of the DREF, under the DREF appeal code MDRID027.

7603.name: Myanmar: Heatwave sEAP, 2024
7603.summary: There has been a general increase in temperatures across Myanmar over the last six decades. This has resulted in an increase in extreme high temperature days and thus the prevalence of heat-related disorders. Prolonged exposure to extreme heat, resulting in heat stress, is expected to increase in the next five years in all regions and states of Myanmar.

7605.name: Bangladesh: Floods EAP, 2024
7605.summary: The Bangladesh Red Crescent Society (BDRCS) has activated its Early Action Protocol (EAP) for Floods. On 9 July, BDRCS convened an EAP ActivationCommittee meeting at 10 am in the BDRCS Emergency Operation Centre (EOC). Based on the analysis the forecast from GLoFAS, the ActivationCommittee agreed that the conditions for activation were sufficiently met for the first trigger of the EAP.

7621.name: Cape Verde - Floods 2025
7621.summary: On the night of 10–11 August 2025, torrential rains triggered devastating flash floods across São Vicente and Santo Antão islands in Cabo Verde, with partial impacts also reported in São Nicolau. The heavy rainfall, occurring within just a few hours, caused widespread flooding, landslides, and extensive destruction of homes, infrastructure, and essential services.

7628.name: Afghanistan : Southeastern and Northern Earthquake, 2025
7628.summary: Situation Afghanistan has experienced two significant earthquakes within a span of two months, compounding humanitarian needs and increasing vulnerability in affected regions. Both events caused widespread destruction to homes and infrastructure, disrupted access to essential services, and left thousands of people in urgent need of assistance ahead of the winter season. On 31 August 2025 at 11:47 PM local time, a 6.0-magnitude earthquake struck southeastern Afghanistan.

7631.name: DRC - Ebola Virus 16 Outbreak - 2025
7631.summary: This is the 16th Ebola Virus Disease (EVD) outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) since 1976. It comes after almost three years without a confirmed outbreak in the country. The previous outbreak was declared on 15 August 2022 in Beni, North Kivu Province, where a single case was reported and later died; the Ministry of Health declared the end of that outbreak on 27 September 2022.

7650.name: Pakistan: Riverine Floods EAP, 2025
7650.summary: Pakistan is a country with diverse landscapes and a fluctuating climate. While typically hot and dry, it has shown significant variations in recent years. The country is prone to hazards such as floods, droughts, cyclones, heatwaves, and earthquakes. Floods occur frequently due to the summer weather system that develops in the Bay of Bengal during the monsoon months of July to September.

7656.name: Philippines: Earthquake and Typhoons 2025
7656.summary: On 30 September 2025 at approximately 9:59 PM local time, a powerful magnitude 6.9 earthquake struck off thecoast of Bogo City, Cebu making it one of the strongest recorded earthquakes in Cebu to date. The epicentre waslocated near Bogo City in northern Cebu with an estimated shallow depth of about five kilometres, where intenseground shaking led to the collapse of buildings, destruction of roads, and power outages.

7658.name: Kenya -  Complex Emergency
7658.summary: Kenya is increasingly vulnerable to climate extremes, with cycles of severe drought often followed by intense rainfall and flooding. Beginning in November 2023, El Niño-enhanced rains triggered widespread flooding that persisted into early 2024, displacing thousands and damaging infrastructure.

7660.name: Somalia -  Complex Emergency
7660.summary: Escalating humanitarian crisis in Puntland and Somaliland: Somalia is facing a rapidly worsening humanitarian crisis in Puntland and Somaliland, where prolonged dry conditions have affected over 2.5 million people across 26 districts including 887,000 people in severely impacted areas. Rural communities are experiencing acute shortages of water and food, compounded by significant funding cuts that have severely weakened the humanitarian response.

7678.name: Jamaica - Hurricane Melissa - October 2025
7678.summary: Hurricane Melissa made landfall in southwestern Jamaica near New Hope as a Category 5 storm with sustained winds of approximately 185 mph (295 km/h), putting it among the most intense Atlantic hurricanes on record, and one of the strongest to hit the island in modern history.Upon striking, the storm brought catastrophic winds, storm surge and torrential rainfall totalling up to 1 000 mm (40 in) in mountainous areas — triggering widespread flooding and landslides.

7687.name: Cuba - Hurricane Melissa - October 2025
7687.summary: Hurricane Melissa rapidly intensified from a tropical wave to a Category 5 storm by 28 October 2025, becoming one of the strongest hurricanes ever recorded in the Caribbean. In response, Cuba activated extensive preparedness measures, including mass evacuations, sheltering, and closures of schools and transportation systems. Over 735,000 people were evacuated prior to the Hurricane making landfall.

7713.name: Sri Lanka - Tropical Cyclone Ditwah, 2025
7713.summary: The flood and landslide situation resulting from Cyclone Ditwah affected an estimated of more than 1.5 million people across the country, and 643 people are reported dead, and 183 people are reported missing (Sri Lanka Brief). According to the UN, the severely affected districts include Gampaha, Colombo, Puttalam, Mannar, Trincomalee, Batticaloa, Kandy, Badulla, Matale, Vavuniya, Kegalle.

7759.name: Mozambique : Floods - 01-2026
7759.summary: Mozambique is experiencing a large-scale flood emergency triggered by persistent and intense rainfall since late December 2025. The Mozambique Red Cross (CVM) has been supporting the Government activation of anticipatory actions with evacuations, distribution of relief items, and dissemination of early warning messages. This was done through the activation of the Floods Early Action Protocol (EAP) and other mechanisms.

7772.name: TUN: Flood - 01-2026 - Tunisia
7772.summary: Since 18 January 2026, eastern and northern Tunisia have been hit by exceptionally heavy rainfall, resulting in widespread flooding across 15 regions and affecting an estimated 25,000 people, including isolated rural and mountainous communities that remain difficult to access.

7796.name: Madagascar - Tropical Cyclones, 2026
7796.summary: Madagascar has experienced successive cyclones that have significantly disrupted access to food, health care, and other essential services for numerous communities. Within a ten-day period, two severe storms intensified an already critical situation. Cyclone Fytia developed on January 28, 2026, made landfall three days later, and traversed Madagascar until February 1.

7826.name: IRN: Complex Emergency - 02-2026 - Iran Complex Emergency
7826.summary: Disaster Overview Since 28 February 2026, Iran has faced a nationwide complex emergency affecting 30 of its 31 provinces, in which direct conflict impacts are amplified by severe economic deterioration, systemic market disruption, and long-standing structural vulnerabilities.

figures.label: IRCS personnel killed while on duty

7831.name: AGO: Flood - 02-2026 - Angola - Floods 2026
7831.summary: During the period of February 21 and 23, heavy rains impacted various municipalities of Cunene province resulting in the following impacts: Houses flooded: 204 Houses damaged: 12 Institutions affected: 18 (9 schools, 6 religious, 3 government buildings) Families reallocated: 204 People impacted: 1,036 people 10km of road impacted Other families lost livelihoods, data unavailable. Most impacted municipalities so far are Cuanhama, followed by Cuvelai and Ombadja.

7833.name: Afghanistan: Complex Emergency, 2026
7833.summary: The ongoing political tension between Afghanistan and Pakistan has turned into clashes between these two countries, which resulted in significant civilian casualties and large-scale displacement in provinces located near the border point of the country (Kuanr, Nuristan, Nangarhar, Paktika, Paktiya, and Khost). As a result, 66 people lost their lives, and 72 were injured. A total of 13,531 families were displaced, while 63 houses were destroyed and 33 were partially damaged.

7862.name: Afghanistan: Flash Floods, 2026
7862.summary: Following heavy and sustained rainfall, flash floods occurred in March 2026 across the country, affecting communities in Helmand, Herat, Badghis, Uruzgan, Samangan, Laghman and Parwan provinces. Low-lying areas and settlements located along riverbeds were particularly impacted.

7878.name: Solomon Islands: Tropical Cyclone Maila, 2026
7878.summary: According to the Solomon Islands Meteorological Service and community reports, storm surge and strong winds have affected parts of Western and Choiseul Provinces. Coastal communities are experiencing sea inundation and rough conditions. Western, Choiseul, Isabel Provinces are in red alerts and Central, Malaita, Guadalcanal, Makira, Temotu, Renell & Bellona Provinces in orange alert. TC Maila category 3 is expected to intensify. Planned assessment in the next few days.

7880.name: PNG: Tropical Cyclone Maila, 2026
7880.summary: Tropical Cyclone Maila is located near 9.6˚S 156.1˚E, with its centre moving north-west at approximately 6km/hour, with maximum gusts at 296km/h. The PNG National Weather Service (NWS) has issued Tropical Cyclone Warning Number 14 (see attached), indicating that Severe Tropical Cyclone Maila (Category 5) continues to affect parts of the country.

7882.name: DOM: Pluvial Flooding / Flood - 04-2026 - Urban and Rural Flooding in Geographical Areas
7882.summary: Wednesday, April 8, 2026 at 6:00 a.m. valid until Friday, April 10, 2026 at 6:00 a.m. HEAVY RAINS WILL PERSIST IN SEVERAL PROVINCES OF THE COUNTRY, DUE TO THE INCIDENCE OF A TROUGH WEATHER WARNING AND ALERT IN FORCE IN SEVERAL PROVINCES OF THE NATIONAL TERRITORY Today, Wednesday, from early in the day, we continue under favorable weather conditions for rainfall to continue in several provinces of the national territory.

7891.name: Malaysia: Sandakan Fire, 2026
7891.summary: A major fire incident occurred in the early hours at Kampung Bahagia, Batu Sapi, Sandakan, resulting in extensive destruction and significant impact on the local community. The incident, which took place at approximately 1:30 a.m., was reported to the authorities and subsequently led to the area being declared a disaster zone at 4:00 a.m. by the relevant authorities.

7910.name: COD: Flood - 05-2026 - Floods in the town of Uvira, South Kivu province in the Democratic Republic of Congo
7910.summary: The rains that fell on the city of Uvira on May 1, 2026 at 10 a.m. in the province of South Kivu in the Democratic Republic of Congo caused material and human damage in the commune of Kalundu in the Nyamianda and Kilibula districts. This situation of flooding exacerbated by climate change and environmental degradation in the city of Uvira has been observed since 2020 by the rise of water in Lake Tanganyika and flash flooding of rivers.

7937.name: Africa - Ebola BVD -  Outbreak 2026
7937.summary: On 15th May, the Institut national de recherche biomédicale (INRB) Kinshasa confirmed an outbreak of the Ebola virus in Ituri province, Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC). The virus is reported to have originated from Mongbwalu, Bunia and Rwapara Health zones in Ituri province. The virus is confirmed to be the Bundibugyo Virus Disease (BVD), a severe and often fatal strain.

7962.name: BULL: Civil unrest - 05-2026 - Civil unrest
7962.summary: The city of El Alto is going through an emergency situation due to the blockades and social protests registered since May 2026, which have interrupted the movement of people and goods. These disturbances have generated shortages of food, fuel and medicines, in addition to the partial suspension of educational and economic activities.

7972.name: ARM: Other - 06-2026 - Severe Hailstorm in Stepanavan
7972.summary: On 6 June 2026, at approximately 12:56 PM, a severe hailstorm struck the Stepanavan community and surrounding areas in Lori Region, Armenia. The hailstorm lasted approximately 15–20 minutes and was accompanied by exceptionally large hailstones, reportedly measuring up to 4–6 cm in diameter. The event caused extensive damage to residential properties, agricultural land, public infrastructure, vehicles, and livestock.

7974.name: Philippines: Maasim, Sarangani Earthquake, 2026
7974.summary: At 7:37 AM on 8 June 2026, a magnitude 7.8 earthquake struck approximately 32 km south 04° west of Maasim, Sarangani, at a depth of 33 kilometers, affecting several areas in Mindanao. The Philippine Institute of Volcanology and Seismology (PHIVOLCS) recorded the strongest shaking at Intensity VII (Destructive) in General Santos City, with expected aftershocks and damages. DOST-PHIVOLCS issued Tsunami Information No.

7977.name: IDN: Drought - 06-2026 - Anticipatory Action: Severe Drought Risk due to El Niño and Positive IOD - Indonesia 2026
7977.summary: Indonesia is forecasted to experience prolonged dry conditions during the 2026 dry season due to the combined influence of El Niño conditions and a positive Indian Ocean Dipole (IOD). According to BMKG, the dry season is expected to begin earlier than normal in many regions, with 57.2% of seasonal zones (ZOM) predicted to experience a longer dry season and 64.5% of Indonesia forecasted to receive below-normal rainfall accumulation during the June–September period.

7979.name: IRQ: Epidemic - 05-2026 - Crimean-Congo Hemorrhagic Fever (CCHF) in Iraq/IRCS
7979.summary: Crimean-Congo Hemorrhagic Fever (CCHF) remains a significant public health concern in Iraq during the 2026 seasonal transmission period. The disease, which is endemic in the country, is primarily associated with exposure to infected ticks, direct contact with infected livestock, and handling of contaminated animal blood and tissues during slaughtering and meat processing activities.

7983.name: MDA: Flood - 05-2026 - Floods in Moldova May-June 2026
7983.summary: The hydrometeorological crisis that affected the Republic of Moldova from late May through mid-June 2026 caused widespread flooding and infrastructure damage across multiple regions, directly affecting an estimated 800–1,000 people. According to information from the General Inspectorate for Emergency Situations (IGSU), the National Crisis Management Center (CNMC), and local authorities, the severe weather impacted communities in 15 districts and municipalities.

7986.name: Malawi - Population Movement 2026
7986.summary: Between March and June, 2026, South Africans started attaching all foreigners pushing them to go out their country. This has resulted in many foreigners being chased from their settlements. This involved included beating, stealling and othe several traumatising situations. Over 9000 Malawian have since assemble at Lindera waiting centre awating to be repatriated to Malawi. Some have already been repatriated to Malawi but the majority are yet to be repatriated.

7987.name: COG: Displacement - 06-2026 - MOVEMENT OF THE POPULATION OF THE DRC IN THE REPUBLIC OF CONGO
7987.summary: On 3 November 2025, a latent land dispute between the Lobalatanda and Engalango Sud communities, in the Dongo sector (Sud-Ubangi, DRC), degenerated into violence after the murder of a teacher perceived as a triggering act. The clashes left five dead, thirteen injured and burned nearly fifty houses around Tomba, forcing residents to flee.

7989.name: Chad - 2026 Cholera Outbreak
7989.summary: The analysis of epidemiological data and field observations reveals the following elements: An epidemic that is still localized but at risk of spread With 52 confirmed cases out of a total population of 124,300 inhabitants, the apparent overall attack rate remains low.

7990.name: Venezuela Earthquake
7990.summary: On 24 June 2026, two strong earthquakes, preliminarily measured at magnitudes 7.1 and 7.5, struck north-central Venezuela in rapid succession, with epicentres near Morón, Carabobo State. The earthquakes were felt across much of the country, including Caracas, La Guaira, Aragua, Carabobo and neighbouring states. Therefore, the national goverment of Venezuela declared the state of emergency.

7998.name: LAO: Flood - 07-2026 - Flooding Caused by Heavy Rainfall
7998.summary: According to the Department of Meteorology and Hydrology (DMH), a tropical depression over the South China Sea is expected to strengthen the south-west monsoon, bringing widespread heavy rainfall, thunderstorms and strong winds across Lao PDR between 2 and 5 July 2026. The forecast indicates an increased risk of flash floods, riverine flooding and landslides, particularly in northern provinces.

8011.name: TJK: Flood - 07-2026 - TJK: Flood and Mudflow Ayni district
8011.summary: On 11 July 2026, following intense rainfall, flash floods and mudflows affected the villages of Darg and Kazdon in Shamtuch Jamoat, Ayni District, Sughd Region. Mudflows descended through the Surkhi, Kashak, and Jari river channels, causing significant damage to residential houses, public infrastructure, road networks, water supply systems, agricultural land, and private property. According to the official authorities, no fatalities or injuries have been reported.

8014.name: KGZ: Pluvial/Flash Flood - 07-2026 - Nooken Mudflow
8014.summary: Executive SummaryOn 13 July 2026 at approximately 19:30 local time, heavy short-duration rainfall in the mountainous areas of Nooken District, Jalal-Abad Oblast triggered mudflows affecting Kochkor-Ata city and surrounding villages. Two mudflow channels overflowed simultaneously: the Besh-Korgon channel inundated residential streets in Kochkor-Ata city and destroyed 3 electricity poles in the Besh-Korgon settlement; the Kara-Bulak channel flooded Ergesh Aliev village.

8022.name: MWI: Epidemic - 07-2026 - Measles Outbreak
8022.summary: The measles outbreak in Nsanje District continues to worsen, affecting several communities, particularly those along the Malawi–Mozambique border. As of 17 July 2026, the district had recorded 188 suspected measles cases, including 76 laboratory-confirmed cases. Children under 15 years of age, particularly those younger than five years, are the most affected.

8025.name: Afghanistan: Nuristan Flood, 2026
8025.summary: On Monday, 20 July 2026, at approximately 3:00 p.m. local time, a sudden flash flood struck the central areas of Nuristan Province following heavy and continuous rainfall. The low-lying areas and communities located along rivers and seasonal watercourses were the most severely affected.

8027.name: DZA: Fire - 07-2026 - Algeria: Wildfires – July 2026
8027.summary: On 18 July 2026, the wildfire emergency in Algeria reached a significant operational peak, with 154 forest, vegetation and agricultural fires recorded within 24 hours across several wilayas. Of these, 138 fires were extinguished, while 16 remained active at the time of reporting.

8038.name: TUN: Fire - 07-2026 - Tunisia Wildfires 2026
8038.summary: The wave of fires in the Republic of Tunisia began on 1 June 2026, but reached a sharp peak from 12 July 2026 onward, continuing to the time of writing, coinciding with an exceptional heatwave in which temperatures reached close to 50°C in several governorates — including Kairouan, Jendouba, Gabès, Tozeur and Béja — while temperatures in the south-west reached around 49°C due to the hot, dry "Chehili" desert winds, according to the National Institute of Meteorology.

8045.name: SLE: Pluvial/Flash Flood - 08-2026 - SLE: Flash Flood - 08-2026 - Freetown
8045.summary: On the early morning of 3 August 2026, Freetown experienced approximately six to seven hours of continuous heavy rainfall, resulting in widespread flash flooding, severe erosion, and slope collapse incidents across several low-lying and hillside communities. The incidents caused significant damage to homes and infrastructure, displaced hundreds of people, resulted in fatalities and missing persons, and contaminated critical water sources.

8055.name: Colombia - Earthquake 2026
8055.summary: According to information from the Colombian Geological Service (SGC), an earthquake with a preliminary magnitude of 7.4 was recorded on Monday, August 10, 2026, in the morning, with its epicenter in the town of San José del Palmar, in the department of Chocó, located on the Colombian Pacific coast, at a depth of 96 kilometers. Although the epicenter was in the department of Chocó, direct impacts were also felt in the departments of Caldas, Risaralda, and Valle del Cauca.

8057.name: Philippines: Southwest Monsoon enhanced by Tropical Cyclones Maymay and Dolphin, 2026
8057.summary: At 8:00 PM on 4 August 2026, the Low-Pressure Area (LPA) located west of Bacnotan, La Union intensified into Tropical Depression MAYMAY, according to the Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration (PAGASA). By 2:00 AM on 5 August 2026, Tropical Depression MAYMAY further intensified into Tropical Storm MAYMAY (international name: Kujira) while moving slowly near the western coast of Northern Luzon.

8062.name: PAN: Flood - 08-2026 - Bocas del Toro Floods
8062.summary: During the afternoon of Sunday, August 16, 2026, the National Civil Protection System (SINAPROC) declared a Green Alert for rain, storms and gusts of wind, starting at 6:00 p.m., for sectors of the province of Bocas del Toro, the Ngäbe-Buglé Region and the Naso Tjër Di Region.

8068.name: Liberia : Floods - 08-2026
8068.summary: Since August 19, 2026, there has been sustained heavy rainfall consistent with the Liberia rainy season, which has caused widespread flash and riverine flooding across seven counties: Montserrado, Cape Mount, Grand Bassa, Bomi, Bong, Rivergss, and Nimba. Montserrado, home to Monrovia ( Liberia's Capital), has a dense urban corridor and the epicenter, with informal settlements along the St. Paul River, StocktonCreek, Du River, and the Mesurado River.

8073.name: Nepal: Rasuwa Flash Flood, 2026
8073.summary: A major flash flood struck Rasuwa district after a sudden and intense surge in the Bhote Koshi River at approximately 9:15 AM. The flood rapidly impacted the Timure, Rasuwagadhi, and Syabrubesi areas, causing significant damage to settlements, markets, police infrastructure, roads, and hydropower facilities. Authorities have warned that rising water levels could affect downstream communities along the Trishuli River corridor.

8078.name: NGA: Population Movement - 08-2026
8078.summary: A joint rapid assessment conducted by the Nigerian Red Cross Society (NRCS), SEMA and Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) from 28–31 August 2026 has identified continued and expanding population movements in Danko-Wasagu and Sakaba LGAs in Zuru Emirate, Kebbi State, confirming that the emerging displacement situation extends beyond the initially affected locations.

8083.name: Yemen Population Movement -2026
8083.summary: The escalation of conflict in Yemen, particularly along the western coast and in Taiz, continues to force families to leave their homes, with many more displaced than once. This is putting additional pressure on host communities and essential services. Families are struggling to meet their basic needs, while insecurity and access restrictions make it difficult to assess the situation and deliver assistance.

8088.name: DJI: Population Movement - 09-2026
8088.summary: Since 10 September 2026, the Obock region has been experiencing a significant influx of people arriving from Yemen, amid a deteriorating security and humanitarian situation in the country. According to estimates shared by ONARS, approximately 1,600 Yemeni refugees, mainly women and children, have arrived in the Obock region to date. Some individuals are reported to have been rescued at sea by the Djiboutian authorities after their boats ran out of fuel.

8090.name: Bangladesh: Dengue Outbreak, 2026
8090.summary: Dengue remains a major public health concern in Bangladesh, with recurrent seasonal outbreaks that threaten life and stretch the health system's capacity. The 2026 outbreak has followed an unusual trajectory: national figures ran below the 2025 pace through mid-August, before a sharp monsoon-driven surge from late August pushed the cumulative case count past last year's comparable tally within weeks.
